scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: HELP! The workstation it_lab3 (one of the IT lab
machines on 192.168.1.x) has turned into a complete BRICK. It can't reach
anything at all, not even its own gateway thing. Its port on the lab switch
has obviously DIED -- the machine is fine, the hole it plugs into is dead,
I'd bet money on it!! Please swap it_lab3 onto a working port (or turn its
port back on) and make it talk to the network again!! The student who uses it
is just sitting there!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
No switchport or network fault found. The it_lab3 workstation is online and fully reachable at both Layer 2 and Layer 3. Direct evidence:
- On it_lab3, eth0 is UP with “Link detected: yes” (ethtool), negotiated 10Gb/s full-duplex. TX/RX counters increment during tests.
- IP config is correct: 192.168.1.5/24 with default route via 192.168.1.1.
- it_lab3 successfully pings its default gateway router0 (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss (≈0.6–0.9 ms) and a same-LAN peer it_lab1 (192.168.1.3) (≈0.25–0.54 ms).
- it_lab3 also reaches another subnet (office_pc 192.168.3.2) through routing with 0% loss (≈1.1–1.4 ms).
- Router0 can ping it_lab3, confirming two-way connectivity.

Mechanism: Because L2 link is up, ARP/ICMP work, and L3 routing via router0 is operational, the path from it_lab3 to local and remote subnets is healthy; a dead switchport would have prevented link detection and all L2/L3 traffic.

Localization: No fault on switch0 access port or router0 eth0; it_lab3’s eth0 is operational.

Root cause: The reported outage cannot be reproduced; there is no network or switchport failure—likely a transient or endpoint/application-layer issue that has since cleared.

Corrective fix: No switchport change required. Have the user re-test. If issues persist with specific apps, check local firewall/DNS/proxy settings on it_lab3 and browser/app configuration, and consider restarting the NIC or host. Network infrastructure requires no action.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes it_lab3 holds its address and reaches its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states it_lab3 has 192.168.1.5/24 and successfully pings its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss.

The agent's logs show it_lab3 has the correct IP and successful ICMP both to its gateway and to an off-segment host, and the host interface is UP—supporting the no-fault conclusion. One small gap is that the ethtool output in the log is truncated so the agent's specific phrasing about negotiated speed/‘Link detected’ is not fully visible, but the core connectivity evidence (ifconfig + bidirectional pings) justifies the diagnosis.
